title: Reliability Acceptance Sampling for Control-Eval Evidence

original_idea.body:
# Reliability Acceptance Sampling for Deciding How Much Control-Eval Evidence Is Enough

**Problem:** Control evals report a safety score from finite episodes but rarely state CIs or required sample sizes. Decisions get made on noisy point estimates.

**Direction:** Import acceptance sampling. Treat each control episode as a pass/fail trial, derive the OC curve and clean-episode count to certify the sabotage rate below a target, then re-analyze published results for evidence strength.

**Why it matters:** Gives control evals a rigorous sample-size framework so safety claims aren't over-read. Statistics-only re-analysis, no compute.

**Relevant context:** MIL-STD-105 OC curves; Ctrl-Z (arXiv:2504.10374); arXiv:2511.02997.
